name: Israel/Lanczos thin-shell junction formalism and the Poisson-Visser shell potential V(R) with the shell conservation law

source.located: PRIMARY: E. Poisson & M. Visser, 'Thin-shell wormholes: Linearization stability', arXiv:gr-qc/9506083v1 (30 Jun 1995), Phys. Rev. D 52, 7318 (1995); eqs (6)-(8) Lanczos/Israel surface stress, (11)-(13) junction + conservation, (14)-(17) Rdot^2 = -V(a), (23) beta^2 = dp/dsigma, (27) V''(a0), (28)-(36) stability region, sec. IV caveats. GENERAL V WITH M_in != M_out (the form the tree actually uses): M. Ishak & K. Lake, 'Stability of transparent spherically symmetric thin shells and wormholes', arXiv:gr-qc/0108058v2, PRD 65, 044011 (2002), eq (5) (credited to K. Lake, PRD 19, 2847 (1979)), eqs (6)-(8) transparency, (14)-(19), sec. III.A-B. Israel 1966 (Nuovo Cimento 44B 1; erratum 48B 463) and Lanczos 1924 are pre-arXiv and are NAMED-NOT-READ; their formalism is read via the exact restatement in Poisson-Visser eqs (3)-(8).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9506083 (all 4 pages returned verbatim) and on gr-qc/0108058 (all 13 pages returned verbatim). Israel/Lanczos: READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (Poisson-Visser sec. II). published_statement: Poisson-Visser (gr-qc/9506083 v1): S^i_j = -(1/8 pi)([K^i_j] - delta^i_j [K]) (6); in spherical symmetry sigma = -(1/4 pi)[K^theta_theta], p = (1/8 pi)([K^tau_tau] + [K^theta_theta]) (8). For two Schwarzschild exteriors of mass M glued at a > 2M: sigma = -(1/2 pi a) sqrt(1-2M/a+adot^2) (11), p = (1/4 pi a)(1 - M/a + adot^2 + a addot)/sqrt(1-2M/a+adot^2) (12); 'It is easy to check that these imply energy conservation: d/dtau(sigma A) + p dA/dtau = 0, A = 4 pi a^2' (13); sigmadot = -2(sigma+p) adot/a (15); 'adot^2 = -V(a); V(a) = 1 - 2M/a - [2 pi sigma(a) a]^2' (17); with beta^2 = dp/dsigma (23), V''(a0) = -2 a0^-2 [2M/a0 + (M^2/a0^2)/(1-2M/a0) + (1+2 beta0^2)(1-3M/a0)] (27); 'So for V''(a0) > 0 the wormhole is stable, while for V''(a0) < 0 perturbations can grow (at least until the nonlinear regime is reached)' (after 28); stable regions I: beta0^2 >= 3/2+sqrt3, a0- < a0 < a0+; II: beta0^2 <= -1/2, a0 > a0- (35)-(36). Sec. IV: 'there is no guarantee that beta0 actually is the speed of sound'. Ishak-Lake (gr-qc/0108058 v2) eq (5): 'Rdot^2 = eps + ([m]/M)^2 - 2 eps mbar/R + (M/2R)^2 ... This is a quadratic identity and applies to both shells and wormholes', M = 4 pi R^2 sigma, [m] = m+ - m-, mbar = (m+ + m-)/2, eps = -1 for timelike Sigma; stability condition V'' > 0 (15); sec. III.B (Brady-Louko-Poisson shell): 'R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0 and R/m+ ~ 3 as m- -> m+' at P'/sigma' = 1.
published_hypotheses: PV-H1 thin (distributional) shell; Einstein equations with the Lanczos/Israel surface stress S^i_j from the jump [K_ij] (PV eqs 3-6)
PV-H2 spherical symmetry; perturbations linearised and spherically symmetric (radial) only (abstract; sec. III)
PV-H3 an ASSUMED static solution (a0, sigma0, p0) with V(a0) = V'(a0) = 0 (eqs 18-20)
PV-H4 an equation of state p = p(sigma) (barotropic), linearised through beta^2 = dp/dsigma at sigma0; beta^2 is a parameter, not necessarily a sound speed (eqs 16, 23; sec. IV)

PV-H5 PV's object specifically: two copies of Schwarzschild EXTERIOR, same M > 0, a0 > 2M, glued as a wormhole (both normals pointing away from the throat); 'it is meaningless to ask what happens for a0 < 2M' (sec. II, III)
PV-H6 stability is LINEAR: V''>0 stable, V''<0 'perturbations can grow (at least until the nonlinear regime is reached)' (after eq 28)
PV-H7 energy conservation (13) is derived from (11)-(12) for vacuum on both sides (no flux term)

IL-H1 general Rdot^2 formula (Lake 1979) is a quadratic identity from squaring the junction condition; valid for shells and wormholes; the sign (orientation) information of K_theta_theta^+- is not carried by the squared form (eqs 3-5)
IL-H2 transparency [G^alpha_beta n_alpha u^beta] = 0 maintained under perturbation, which with static vacuum embeddings reduces to the PV conservation law (eqs 6-8, sec. II.C)
IL-H3 Upsilon = 8 pi R^2 (sigma + P) != 0 (no domain-wall asymptote) for the beta^2 parametrisation of the stability boundary (sec. II.D)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (class widened, legitimately): linstab.py:208-211 (P1-P2) and stability.py:16-19,40-43 apply the machinery to a SHELL with Schwarzschild M_in = -m < 0 inside and Minkowski outside. Poisson-Visser's paper treats only the equal-mass Schwarzschild WORMHOLE (PV-H5); the potential V = 1 - 2M_out/R - ((M_out-M_in)/m_s - m_s/(2R))^2 used at linstab.py:512 is Lake's identity, Ishak-Lake eq (5) with eps = -1 (re-derived: check 1a from the squared Israel condition, 1b against IL eq (5)). The identity is stated for general m+-, and the rederivation holds for M_in < 0 (check 3a samples M_in down to -3), so the widening is SUPPORTED; the attribution 'Poisson-Visser: ... V(R) = ...' at stability.py:40 (and 'poisson_visser' as the function name at linstab.py:507) is an ATTRIBUTION DISCREPANCY -- PV supply the beta^2 linearisation method, Lake/Ishak-Lake the two-mass potential -- recorded, not a mathematical error.

DROPPED (named here, satisfied on the object): the orientation/sign conditions lost when the junction condition is squared (IL-H1). The squared V is equivalent to the Israel equations only where sqrt(f_out + Rdot^2) = (M_out-M_in)/m_s - m_s/(2R) > 0 and sqrt(f_in + Rdot^2) = (M_out-M_in)/m_s + m_s/(2R) > 0 (outward normals on both sides). linstab.py:208-214 lists P1-P4 without it. On the device static shell these equal exactly 1 and u (check 4h), both > 0, so they hold in a neighbourhood and the linear result is unaffected; a statement of P1 that is complete would name them.

DROPPED (named here, not entering the l = 0 result): the idealised interior 'Schwarzschild M_in = -m ... no horizon' (linstab.py:209-210, stability.py:18) extended to r -> 0 contains the negative-mass Schwarzschild curvature singularity at r = 0, which is naked (timelike). P2 names the absence of a horizon, not the singular centre. For P3's l = 0 sector the shell equation depends only on f_in(R) (Birkhoff: static vacuum interior), so the radial result does not use the centre; for any l >= 1 analysis (the NOT-RUN list) boundary conditions at r = 0 would be an additional hypothesis. linstab.py:215-219 already records that concentric.py's actual device replaces the centre with a Plummer core, so this concerns only the idealisation.

rederivation.outcome: 24/24 checks pass (sympy exact + z3 nonlinear real arithmetic + mpmath). Built independently of linstab.py: (1a) the tree's V equals V derived from the Israel condition sqrt(f_in+Rdot^2) - sqrt(f_out+Rdot^2) = m_s/R; (1b) equals Ishak-Lake eq (5), eps = -1; (2a,2b) the tree's sigma0 and p0 are the Lanczos values in PV's eq (8) convention; (2c) the static family satisfies m_s0' = -8 pi R p0 identically; (2d) conservation gives sigma' = -2(sigma+p)/R (PV 15); (3a) V(R0) = V'(R0) = 0 on 40 random (M_in, M_out) incl. M_in < 0; (4a,4b) the device V''(R0) = [2 beta^2 (3u+1) u^2 + (u-1)(3u^2+2u+1)/2]/(u^2 R^2) and beta^2_crit = -(u-1)(3u^2+2u+1)/(4u^2(3u+1)) exactly as linstab.py:33-34; (4c) the beta^2 coefficient 2(3u+1) > 0 so stability iff beta^2 > beta^2_crit; (4d,4e) limits -1/4 (u->oo) and 0 (u->1); (4f) z3: -1/4 < beta^2_crit < 0 for every u > 1; (4g) z3: strictly decreasing (d/du numerator -2(3u^3+3u^2+5u+1)); (4h) the dropped sign conditions hold at the static device shell (B = 1, A = u); (4j) the ordinary shell (M_in = 0, M_out = M) gives the same V'' and beta^2_crit with u -> s = sqrt(1-2M/R) (DEVICE_IS_WALL_FORMULA_AT_U). Machinery validated against PUBLISHED numbers: (5a) ordinary shell at beta^2 = 1: R/M = 2.370393, Ishak-Lake 'R/m+ ~ 2.37 as m- -> 0'; (5b) m-/m+ = 0.999999: R/m+ = 2.9999985, Ishak-Lake '~ 3 as m- -> m+'; (5c,5d) PV eq (27) V''(a0) and V(a0) = V'(a0) = 0 re-derived exactly for the wormhole; (5e,5f) PV eq (33) and its discriminant roots 3/2 +- sqrt3 re-derived; (5g) ordinary-shell beta^2_crit converted by Gamma = beta^2 (sigma+p)/p equals the LeMaitre-Poisson Gamma_1 = (4 - 6C + 2 sqrt(1-2C))/(4(1-2C)) EXACTLY (sympy zero) -- formula taken from the tree's quotation at wall.py:110-116, not read at source here. Side note, recorded not repaired: in float64 the 5g comparison shows a 1.3e-4 residual at C = 1e-6 from cancellation in p ~ C^2; the identity is exact, so wall.py's '1e-15 at every x from 1e-6' is not reproduced in float64 by this script's naive route but is true of the exact identity.

later_literature.ref: Pitre, Schneider & Poisson, 'Self-gravitating thin shells are dynamically unstable on all angular scales', arXiv:2604.05980 (2026)
later_literature.what: Per its abstract (discover_papers) and the tree's restatement (wall.py:110-126): a static thin perfect-fluid shell with barotropic EOS, Minkowski inside and Schwarzschild outside, has an unstable even-parity mode for all sampled compactness, adiabatic index and l >= 2; its radial criterion Gamma >= Gamma_1 agrees with the PV-type radial result (reproduced exactly here, check 5g, from the quoted formula). This narrows what 'stable' can mean -- radial (PV) stability does not imply stability -- but does not touch the tree's l = 0 statement, which is scoped to P3 and keeps l >= 1 NOT-RUN. Its configuration has M_in >= 0; whether the l >= 2 mode survives M_in < 0 is the tree's open item (stability.py:80-90), not settled by this paper.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: Poisson-Visser (1995) and Ishak-Lake (2002) used NO measured data -- the results are identities of classical GR with a distributional source, parametrised by M/a0 and beta^2. There is therefore no datum they lacked whose later value could move the conclusion; the re-derivation here reproduces every printed formula exactly (PV eqs 27, 33 and discriminant; IL eq 5 and sec. III.B numbers). What they lacked is not data but (i) a microphysical model fixing beta^2 -- PV sec. IV say so explicitly, and it is still absent; the tree correctly treats beta^2 as a free EOS parameter and states its result for all beta^2 > beta^2_crit; and (ii) the NON-RADIAL analysis, which arrived in 2026 (Pitre-Schneider-Poisson) and shows radial stability does not imply stability for positive-mass interiors. (ii) narrows the reach of 'stable', not the l = 0 statement the tree makes. Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: exact agreement of 24 checks, including two independently published numbers (2.37, 3) and a 2019/2026 independent radial criterion (Gamma_1), with nothing measured entering.
grade_evidence: For the statement and hypotheses AS USED (linstab.py:208-214, 508-524: thin shell, spherical symmetry, l = 0 linear perturbations, barotropic beta^2, vacuum on both sides): the potential V is exactly the squared Israel junction condition and Lake/Ishak-Lake eq (5); sigma0, p0 are exactly the Lanczos values; m_s' = -8 pi R p is exact for vacuum/vacuum; V = V' = 0 at the static shell; the device's V'' and beta^2_crit are reproduced exactly and z3 proves -1/4 < beta^2_crit < 0 and strict decrease for every u > 1; the machinery reproduces PV eq (27)/(33), Ishak-Lake's 2.37 and 3, and Gamma_1 exactly. No datum enters. Recorded, not grade-moving: (a) attribution discrepancy -- the two-mass V is Lake's (Ishak-Lake eq 5), not in Poisson-Visser, who treat only the equal-mass wormhole (stability.py:40, linstab.py:507); (b) two unnamed hypotheses the tree should name -- the orientation sign conditions lost on squaring (verified true on the device, check 4h) and the singular r = 0 of the idealised negative-mass interior (irrelevant at l = 0 by Birkhoff; relevant to any l >= 1 work). Neither shrinks the class on which the tree's l = 0 conclusion holds, so the grade is STANDS, not NARROWED. Scope carried with the grade: STANDS means LINEAR RADIAL stability in PV's sense; later literature (2604.05980, not read here) shows radial stability does not imply stability for positive-mass shells, which the tree already leaves NOT-RUN.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree's use were read beyond l = 0 or beyond linear order (e.g. 'the device is stable' without 'radial, linear'), or if a configuration were priced where the orientation conditions fail (sqrt(f_out+Rdot^2) = [m]/m_s - m_s/2R <= 0, e.g. a shell past the maximal-slice turning point) while still using the squared V; WRONG only if a counterexample to the exact identities above were shown (none exists: sympy returns zero); OPEN would apply to the l >= 2 question for M_in < 0, which is not part of this result. Reading 2604.05980 at source could change the later-literature entry's read_status, not this grade.
